orientation.interpretation: No strong simple tip-state separation in the common Japan-only four-climate panel. This does not replace the separately frozen transition-level orientation analysis.

phyllary.reason: Only one appressed taxon is represented at the primary >=3-occurrence gate.

stickiness.interpretation: Sticky taxa occupy wetter current niches in this Japan provenance frame, with the strongest single-axis separation on BIO12. Because four climate axes were frozen and examined together, BIO12 is a focused lead rather than a standalone confirmatory claim; the omnibus four-climate rank is 9.52%.

phyllary_min1.interpretation: Lowering occurrence depth does not solve state replication; both appressed and spreading remain single-lineage states.

cross_trait_conclusion: The three historical traits can now be passed through one common present-environment pipeline. Their ecological evidence is not equivalent: orientation lacks strong simple tip-state separation in the common Japan panel but has a separately established transition-level signal; stickiness has a replicated 6-vs-6 current-niche panel with a precipitation lead; phyllary remains public-data resolution-limited because state replication is inadequate.
claim_boundary: Present-environment correspondence is not adaptation, selection or historical cause.
Taxon-level authority states are not measured at each occurrence coordinate.
The BIO12 stickiness rank is one of four frozen climate axes and should not be presented as an unadjusted discovery without its omnibus/multiplicity context.
Phyllary coverage failure is a resolution result, not evidence of no ecological relationship.
Japan is a provenance frame for matching the Japan38 phylogeny, not a biological region class.
